newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech miners, power firm seek govt energy plan.
newsitem.headline: Czech miners, power firm seek govt energy plan.

text.p: Major Czech electricity producer CEZ a.s. and coal mining companies on Wednesday called on the state to form a long-term energy supply policy to help them make investment decisions.

Speaking at a joint news conference, representatives of CEZ, miners Severoceska Doly a.s., Sokolovska Uhelna a.s., and Mostecka Uhelna Spolecnost a.s. called on the government to form a policy that would last beyond the year 2020.
"It is necessary to have signals as a basis for decision making," said Miroslav Vlcek of CEZ.
He added that the declaration of an energy policy should include a decision on further privatisation in the sector, the rate of energy imports, prices, and the form of future energy production.
The Industry and Trade Ministry has been mulling a similar proposal, but has yet to submit it to cabinet for approval.
The brown coal miners, who supply CEZ's power plants in northern regions of the country, criticised the cabinet's decision at the beginnning of the 1990's to ban mining at some surface mines.

Extensive mining activity and construction of heavily polluting coal-burning power plants during the communist period turned the north-west part of the country into one of the most devastated parts of Europe.

But the miners argued on Wednesday that the country should not opt for imports of fuels in the future such as natural gas instead of burning coal, saying new power production technologies limited dangerous emissions.
CEZ is building a nuclear power plant at Temelin in the southern Czech Republic which should replace some blocs in its ageing brown coal-fuelled power stations.
Any plants which remain open must be equipped with cleaning devices by the end of the next year.
